q: 1. In paints, pigment is responsible for .............
explain: Pigments are finely ground solid particles that provide the paint with its color, opacity, and some protection against UV rays.

q: 2. The chief ingredient of a paint is .............
explain: While the vehicle (oil) holds the paint together, the pigment is considered the chief ingredient as it provides color and protection.

q: 3. The liquid medium used in oil paints is .............
explain: Linseed oil is the most common vehicle (binder) used in oil-based paints because it dries into a tough, transparent film.

q: 4. The pigment in paints is mixed to give desired .............
explain: The primary function of a pigment in paint is to impart the desired color and opacity to the finished surface.

q: 5. The liquid part of the paint is called .............
explain: The vehicle (or binder) is the liquid part of the paint that carries the pigment in suspension and binds it to the surface.

q: 6. The liquid medium used in enamel paints is .............
explain: Enamel paints are made by adding pigments to varnish. This gives them a hard, glossy, and durable finish.

q: 7. The metallic oxide used in the form of powder in a paint is called .............
explain: The base is a metallic oxide (like white lead or zinc oxide) which is the principal constituent of a paint, making it opaque and durable.

q: 8. The base in a paint is added to .............
options: hide the surface to be painted
explain: The base provides the 'body' to the paint and is responsible for making the paint film opaque so it can hide the surface being painted.

q: 9. The commonly base used in a paint is .............
explain: White lead, zinc oxide, and titanium white are all common bases used depending on the desired finish and exposure conditions.

q: 10. The thinner used for oil paints is .............
explain: Turpentine is a volatile liquid used as a thinner to reduce the viscosity of oil-based paints, making them easier to apply.

q: 11. Linseed oil in paint is used as a .............
explain: Linseed oil acts as the carrier or vehicle, holding the pigments in suspension and forming a solid film once dried.

q: 12. Linseed oil is rapidly soluble in .............
explain: As per Key D.Turpentine is the standard solvent for thinning and dissolving linseed oil in traditional painting practices.

q: 13. The commonly used extender in a paint is .............
explain: Extenders (like barium sulphate, gypsum, or silica) are inert materials added to paint to increase its volume and reduce costs without changing its properties significantly.

q: 14. The drier in an oil paint should not be more than ......... (by volume).
explain: Excessive drier can make the paint film brittle and cause it to peel. The standard limit is 10% by volume.

q: 15. The commonly used solvent in oil paints is .............
explain: Both turpentine and naphtha (mineral spirits) are commonly used as solvents/thinners in oil-based paints.

q: 16. Galvanizing means covering iron with a thin coat of .............
explain: Galvanization is the process of applying a protective zinc coating to iron or steel to prevent rusting.

q: 17. A prime coat is given to steel work with ............
options: a mixture of white lead and lead paint
explain: As Per Book key B is answer but as per google Red oxide of iron is the standard primer used for steel structures to inhibit rust and provide a surface for subsequent paint layers.

q: 18. The base material for distemper, is ............
explain: Distemper is essentially a water-based paint where whiting (powdered chalk) is the primary solid base material.

q: 19. Putty is made up of ............
options: powdered chalk and raw linseed oil
zinc oxide and boiled linseed oil
explain: Glazing putty is prepared by mixing finely powdered chalk (whiting) with raw linseed oil until it reaches a dough-like consistency.

q: 20. Timber can be made more fire resistant by ............
options: hot and cold open tank treatment
explain: Sir Abel's process involves coating timber with sodium silicate and slaked lime, which provides a fire-resistant layer.

q: 21. Brass is an alloy of ............
explain: Brass is composed of Copper and Zinc. Bronze, by contrast, is primarily Copper and Tin.

q: 22. The best primer used for structural steel work is ............
explain: Red lead is traditionally considered the superior primer for structural steel because it provides excellent corrosion inhibition.

q: 23. The vehicle used in bronze paints is usually ............
explain: Metallic paints like bronze paint typically use a specialized vehicle like nitro-cellulose lacquer to prevent the metallic pigment from tarnishing.

q: 24. The pigment used in paints for corrosive resistance, is ............
explain: Red lead is widely used as a primer on iron and steel surfaces because of its excellent anti-corrosive properties.

q: 25. The material generally not used as extender in paints is ............
explain: Zinc white is a pigment (it provides color and opacity), whereas powdered silica, gypsum, and talc are inert fillers used as extenders.

q: 26. The commonly used thinner in oil paints, is ............
explain: Turpentine and Naptha  is the most common thinner used in oil-based paints to adjust the consistency and facilitate easy application.

q: 27. Spirit varnish generally consists of ............
explain: Spirit varnish is made by dissolving resins like shellac or lac in methylated spirit (alcohol).

q: 28. Oil varnish generally consists of ............
explain: Oil varnish is prepared by dissolving hard resins in linseed oil and thinning the mixture with turpentine.

q: 29. Stucco are suitable for ............
explain: Stucco is a type of plaster used for coating exterior walls and surfaces, providing a decorative and protective layer over both stone and brick masonry.

q: 30. German silver is and alloy of ............
explain: German silver contains no actual silver; it is an alloy of Copper, Nickel, and Zinc, named for its silver-like appearance.
